hints: Watch which way the arrow points. It turns the same amount each time.
Compare the 1st and 2nd arrows. The arrow made a quarter turn in the direction a clock's hands move (clockwise).
Each step is a quarter turn clockwise: left, up, right, down. Turn the last arrow (↓) one more quarter turn clockwise.

solution.methodName: Check one change at a time

steps.action: Check how the arrow turns: ← to ↑ to → to ↓.
steps.why: Every figure is one arrow, so only its direction changes.

steps.action: Each step is a quarter turn (90°) clockwise, the way a clock's hands move.
steps.why: Picture a clock: the hand goes from 9 to 12 to 3 to 6. That is left, up, right, down.

steps.action: Turn ↓ a quarter turn clockwise. It now points left.
steps.why: On the clock, after 6 comes 9 again. After a full turn, the arrow is back where it started.

trapNotes.↑: ↑ points the opposite way to ↓, which is a half turn. Each step is only a quarter turn.
trapNotes.↙: ↙ is only an eighth of a turn (45°) from ↓. Each step in this series is a quarter turn (90°).
trapNotes.→: → is a quarter turn the wrong way (counterclockwise). The arrow has been turning clockwise: left, up, right, down.
